summary: 30 complete documentation guides and 52 additional screened creative-AI tools/components. 11 earlier screened entries now have guides; these are review completions, not new-launch claims. Workflows include editable agent-authored pixel assets, game art, transcript-based editing, local music sketches, typography/story prompting, OCR and VFX handoff. Every admission has a complete current software-grant review and six explicit quality checks. Required proprietary hosts, restricted/unclear weights and paid services are separated from the code license. Nothing discovered was installed or run. Final query metadata adds textile reconstruction, local filmmaking, agent capture/synchronization and depth-based temporal VFX. A WIF matrix round-trip is not a physical cloth trial, relative depth is not metric geometry, and MiniMax-H3 territory/output terms and Qwen-Image2.1 noncommercial terms are separate from the application’s open code grant. An audio-to-MIDI/ML roadmap without the implemented AI feature stays local. Nine existing-library source follow-ups recover five complete software grants from GitLab without promoting their quality tiers; one current low-poly portrait repository contains only README and LICENSE, so its setup check is explicitly failed. Codeberg bot challenges and unavailable OpenSlides sources keep affected checks unknown. The prior 3000-entry library already has this week’s cited whole-library source reviews; these follow-ups and new records extend that coverage, rather than claiming3000 new reviews today. Final weekly completeness is checked after the library refresh. The full frozen discovery plan covers 108 fields,1177 repository queries and 27 model tasks. It carries every prior term/lane, adds an agent-pixel-art field, event-camera/caustic terms and image classification/feature extraction, deepens74 formerly bounded queries and adds120 date partitions for 40 capped terms. All three repository lanes remain active. Live primary research beyond GitHub supplements every field and all eight configured ecosystems. Metadata-level screening includes the complete retained catalog and historical pilot entries, followed by targeted document/code/full-license reviews beyond the automatic README shortlist; raw unreviewed/excluded records stay local. Two earlier unsealed Codeberg bot-challenge bodies were superseded during recapture; their original attempt metadata is retained with that archival limitation. Later challenge captures and failed source requests are preserved, and no quality or license claim relies on the missing bodies. First-hand support reports add concrete Windows plugin-discovery, ComfyUI setup, EXR color metadata, DXF and cached-model caveats. Owner examples, agent judges, stars and source activity do not establish a recommendation. The Aseprite plugin is represented as optional packaging around its canonical server rather than counted twice. Web/manual shells, source failures and bounded captures are disclosed; retained research abstracts supply context without a claim of complete paper or manual review today. There is no fixed profile/discovery quota, platform preference, app execution or extra scheduler.  Verified collection: 1177/1177 repository queries attempted; 1174 successful, 2 partial, 1 failed and 255 bounded/truncated. All 27 model tasks were attempted; 0 failed. These are bounded discovery attempts, not an exhaustive census or quality approval. Empty model-source responses: text2text-generation. An empty response does not establish that these creative workflows have no tools. Separate from successful search queries, 53 watchlist fetches and 4 enrichment attempts failed; the detailed warnings remain in the report. A 404/409 is an availability gap, not proof of abandonment or license revocation.

introduction.text: An AI agent authors and patches editable palette-based JSON through CLI or MCP tools; Pixelbolt deterministically rasterizes sprites, scenes and animations and returns pixel grids/contact sheets for the next agent revision. good_for.text: Making small editable sprites, tiles, interface icons and short pixel effects, with exact palette revisions and transparent exports for games or video composition.

demo.text: The owner supplies source recipes, animated galleries and a controlled comparison on older version 0.11.0. That study did not meet its preregistered threshold for claiming an advantage over direct agent coding; it is not independent proof of current 0.17 output quality. Inspect every frame and loop at native resolution.

installation.text: Use the official portable Studio archive for Windows x64, Linux x64/ARM64 or macOS Intel/Apple Silicon, or clone the source with Node 20+. The portable build bundles Node 24 LTS. No npm install or image-model download is needed for the renderer. Connect your chosen AI host separately; the optional skills CLI has a distinct Node 22.20+ requirement and telemetry behavior.

usage.text: Start with a short, representative project and inspect the result before a larger batch.
steps: Open the local studio, choose a small supplied recipe and save your own JSON copy.
Have your agent alter a palette, one region or a short motion; validate the recipe and inspect its native-size frames, silhouette and loop.
Render into a new output folder, keeping the JSON recipe and atlas with the PNG/APNG assets. GIF export can alter alpha and timing.
For a video editor, export a constant-rate numbered PNG sequence and set that rate on import. Pixelbolt supplies FFmpeg commands but does not itself encode an MP4.

Choose the backend/model explicitly. Missing faster-whisper models download from Hugging Face. Open the SRT in Tero with the corresponding local media and revise text, timing, segmentation and export format.

For integrated transcription, the inspected Audio to text form has Engine, Model, Language and Track controls, a model-download button, Generate, and load-after/add-while-transcribing choices. Its implementation rejects HTTP media for this operation and requires FFmpeg and the selected backend; use a local file.

For code-switched speech, the documented faster-whisper mixed-language option detects each 30-second window; do not force one language for the whole clip. Translate to English changes the task and is distinct from transcription in the source language.

Check quiet lines, noise, repetitions and speaker attribution against the original audio. Preserve a revised subtitle copy and verify timing/line breaks in the target player; an automatic QC profile does not certify accessibility or translation quality.

steps: Open a short local video. Start with the basic cube to check decoding and choose its In/Out range; brightness-derived relief is a conventional fallback, not AI depth.
Choose Build AI depth, wait for its separate model download/build and inspect depth edges. The current code uses LiheYoung/depth-anything-large-hf, rather than assuming this is Depth Anything V2.

Try Depth points or Depth sheets. For subject isolation, pause on a clear object, Find it with text or click a point, then Follow it; the tracker may release the object when it leaves or becomes uncertain.

Use Camera path only as an artistic estimate: the default 65-degree field of view is assumed, and depth is relative. Orbit/Walk/Turn are synthetic paths and are explicitly different from the measured-from-video option.

Choose frame-by-frame export for a plate. Opaque export is H.264 MP4; the documented transparent route is ProRes 4444 MOV or VP9-alpha WebM. Live Record stays opaque. Check alpha, timing, contours and sound in the actual receiving editor.
